title: Power Apps: build model-driven apps with Copilot Cowork
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements, and documented control paths and calls are supported. The updated Dataverse capacity documentation supports the storage statements, and the briefing distinguishes the planned model-driven app skill from other documented Cowork app-building experiences.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Cowork access is granted to users within a spending policy's scope when that policy selects Cowork.
claims.quote: A user has access to Cowork when a policy's scope includes them (directly through All users, or through a security group) and that policy selects Cowork under Select agents and services.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: A low credit limit does not block access to Cowork.
claims.quote: Any user in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork can use Cowork, regardless of how small the credit limit is. A policy with a limit of one credit still grants access.

claims.claim: Removing a user from every spending policy that includes Cowork removes that user's Cowork access.
claims.quote: To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork.

claims.claim: Configuration of the Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents has no effect on who can use Cowork.
claims.quote: The Cowork agent entry is still visible under Agents > All Agents, but any configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork.

claims.claim: Credit limits are not a real-time access gate, so users may start tasks after reaching a limit.
claims.quote: Credit limits are a spending safeguard, not a real-time access gate. Credit consumption and limit enforcement are evaluated asynchronously, so a user might be able to start one or more tasks after their limit is reached before enforcement takes effect.

claims.claim: The System Administrator security role provides the required role-assignment privileges by default.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment security roles are an existing Power Platform mechanism for controlling a user's permissions.
claims.quote: Security roles control a user's access to data through a set of access levels and permissions. The combination of access levels and permissions that are included in a specific security role sets limits on the user's view of data and on the user's interactions with that data.
